title: A live sales tile on a shop owner's dashboard
summary: Show today's sales updating on a dashboard without the page hammering the server or lying.
context: Kadlekai Kart's web dashboard shows shop owners today's sales, top items and low stock. Owners leave it open on a counter computer all day, and 15,000 of them may be connected in the evening.

It polls every five seconds for every tile, which accounts for a third of all server traffic, yet owners still say the figure disagrees with the sales list. Connections sometimes drop for hours and return.
must_handle: A sale appears on the tile within about ten seconds.
A background tab stops costing the server anything.
The tile and the list below it do not contradict each other.
After a long drop the page recovers by itself.
A tile that is out of date looks out of date.
show_in_answer: Which data each tile needs, and how fresh it must be.
How updates get to the browser, and why that way.
How the client state is kept together, so that the tile and the list agree.
What each failure looks like to the owner.
